Scheduled messages to yourself should be marked as unread

In general, when a user sends a message, that message is automatically marked as read for the sender. However, in the special case when a user **schedules** a DM to themselves (no other recipients), the message should be marked as unread when it's received. This serves a common use case for scheduling such a message, which is setting yourself a reminder.

[CZO discussion](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/101-design/topic/scheduled.20messages.20to.20yourself/near/1566119)

Delete notification bot messages for resolved topics, on undo in a short grace period

When you (un)resolve a topic, we send an automated notification noting that it was resolved.  This can be unfortunate in the event of a misclick, since one ends up creating two spam messages. Rather than making it harder to resolve topics, we'd like to instead design a grace period. We'd modify `maybe_send_resolve_topic_notifications` to add the following logic:
* If the newest message that was moved is a notification bot "marked as resolved" message (so there's no conversation that might be made confusing).
* And that message's timestamp is within settings.RESOLVE_TOPIC_UNDO_GRACE_PERIOD_SECONDS, which defaults to 60 seconds but should be 5 seconds in a development environment environment (to make it easier to test the unresolve functionality without waiting a minute).
* Then we'd delete the "marked as resolved" notice rather than adding a new one that says the opposite by calling `do_delete_messages` on the notice.

(And presumably the opposite for if you accidentally toggled in the other direction).

Update `Draft` schema in OpenAPI documentation.

Currently, the `Draft` object schema in the OpenAPI documentation includes an `id` property by default. There are two endpoints (found here in the documentation: [`api/create drafts`](https://zulip.com/api/create-drafts) and [`api/edit-draft`](https://zulip.com/api/edit-draft)) that reference this schema in the documentation, but where that property should not be present in the object being sent from the client.

Tusd integration fails S3 credential assertion with IAM roles, leading to failed uploads

After upgrading from Zulip server 9.2 -> 10.0, uploads began failing with the following log in /var/log/zulip/tusd.log:

```
2025-03-21 05:39:41.600 INFO [botocore.credentials] Found credentials from IAM Role: REDACTED
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/zulip/deployments/current/manage.py", line 150, in <module>
    execute_from_command_line(sys.argv)
  File "/home/zulip/deployments/current/manage.py", line 115, in execute_from_command_line
    utility.execute()
  File "/home/zulip/deployments/2025-03-21-05-12-20/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/core/management/__init__.py", line 436, in execute
    self.fetch_command(subcommand).run_from_argv(self.argv)
  File "/home/zulip/deployments/2025-03-21-05-12-20/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/core/management/base.py", line 413, in run_from_argv
    self.execute(*args, **cmd_options)
  File "/home/zulip/deployments/2025-03-21-05-12-20/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/django/core/management/base.py", line 459, in execute
    output = self.handle(*args, **options)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/zulip/deployments/2025-03-21-05-12-20/zerver/management/commands/runtusd.py", line 62, in handle
    assert settings.S3_KEY is not None
```

runtusd.py expects `settings.S3_KEY` and `settings.S3_SECRET_KEY` to be set in order to upload to S3. However, in the case of AWS IAM roles, the credentials can be transparently loaded from the local instance's metadata url. In this case, they would not be explicitly configured, and would be loaded automatically by boto3:
> Note that if you’ve launched an EC2 instance with an IAM role configured, there’s no explicit configuration you need to set in Boto3 to use these credentials. Boto3 will automatically use IAM role credentials if it does not find credentials in any of the other places listed previously.

The Zulip File Uploads Backends documentation also explicitly supports this:
> Set s3_key and s3_secret_key in /etc/zulip/zulip-secrets.conf to be the S3 access and secret keys for the IAM account. **Alternately**, if your Zulip server runs on an EC2 instance, **set the IAM role for the EC2 instance to the role**.

As a workaround, I've commented out the following lines in runtusd.py to avoid the explicit credential checking and passing:
```python
assert settings.S3_KEY is not None
assert settings.S3_SECRET_KEY is not None

env_vars["AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"] = settings.S3_KEY
env_vars["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] = settings.S3_SECRET_KEY
```

Tusd is using the AWS Go SDK, which also properly loads the instance's credentials without having to be explicitly passed them.
> Credentials can also be loaded from a shared credentials file (~/.aws/credentials) as described in the [AWS SDK for Go](https://aws.github.io/aws-sdk-go-v2/docs/configuring-sdk/#specifying-credentials). You still need to declare the AWS_REGION value which isn’t conventionally associated with credentials.

Display which user group was mentioned in email/mobile push notifications

As a follow-up to https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/13074#discussion_r317743329, we should extend our display logic for mentions of user groups to support e.g. "Hamlet mentioned @mobile" if that's what happened, rather than the current "Hamlet mentioned you".  And similarly for the text in emails: "You are receiving this because you were mentioned" -> "You are receiving this because @mobile was mentioned".

There's a few stages required to make this work:
* This block of code in `do_send_messages` is where we drop the information for which user group(s) were mentioned and just turn it into a set of mentioned users:
```
        for group_id in message['message'].mentions_user_group_ids:
            members = message['mention_data'].get_group_members(group_id)
            message['message'].mentions_user_ids.update(members)
```

We need to process that data in a more complex fashion to output a few values:
* The set of users who are mentioned and need a notification
* The mapping from `user_id -> {"personal mention", user_group_id}`.

One plausible way to do that would be to replace `mentions_user_ids` with a `Dict` mapping the user ID to either `True` (for personal mention) or the `user_group_id`; depending on how the user was mentioned in this message.  If a user's mentioned multiple ways, we use the highest priority (personal over user group) and a random user group (doesn't matter which).  The benefit of this model is that we don't have to change most downstream code that just looks at keys in `mentions_user_ids`.

We'd then extend this data set with a `mentioned_group: user_group_id` value in the case a user group is involved:

```
        users = [
            dict(
                id=user_id,
                flags=user_flags.get(user_id, []),
                always_push_notify=(user_id in message['push_notify_user_ids']),
                stream_push_notify=(user_id in message['stream_push_user_ids']),
                stream_email_notify=(user_id in message['stream_email_user_ids']),
            )
            for user_id in user_ids
        ]
```

We pass that data on to `maybe_enqueue_notifications` as a new argument `mention_user_group_id = mentioned_users.get(user_id, False)` (so we have True/False,user_group_id).

13074 is a good template for how to test the downstream flow from there -- we basically just want that value to make it through to the `push_notifications.py` and `email_notifications.py` code to be used in the formatting conditionals.

Add a stronger assertion that database migrations are identical between source and destination Zulip servers for imports

The fix is likely to write out a file containing the set of migrations applied into the export tarballs and diff them ... with care taken to avoid breakage related to different sets of apps being installed (E.g. According to the [OpenAPI specification](https://swagger.io/specification/), a parameter like

```yaml
      - name: messages
        in: query
        description: An array containing the IDs of the target messages.
        schema:
          type: array
          items:
            type: integer
        example: [4, 8, 15]
        required: true
```

should actually serialize as `messages=4,8,15` rather than `messages=[4, 8, 15]`. Since we’re expecting the latter, this parameter should have been defined as

```yaml
      - name: messages
        in: query
        description: An array containing the IDs of the target messages.
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: array
              items:
                type: integer
        required: true
```

I’m not sure whether whether the `example` should be written `[4, 8, 15]` or `"[4, 8, 15]"` (or perhaps it should be `[4, 8, 15]` but indented to be a child of `schema`).

The current `test_openapi` doesn’t accept this, so it needs to be fixed to accept the correct definition and ideally reject the incorrect one.

Make API for message edit history more friendly for clients

Currently, message edit history is a pain to work with, because the optimized data structure we use on the backend only records the **previous** stream and topic values.  What this means is you need to run effectively a reverse loop through the topics/streams if you ever want to compare the values, e.g. to determine if there's ever been a "resolve topic" transaction.  (You basically need to infer that the new topic is the `prev_subject` value of the next edit history event that has one, or if there isn't one, the current subject of the message).

Having thought about it a bit, I think the right way to fix this is as follows:
* First, add a database migration that does this loop once and changes the format of `message_edit_history` entries in the database to (A) be a Postgres JSONB field and (B) extend the existing edit history entries with `topic` and `new_stream_id` fields (name needs confirmation).  In that same migration, we can potentially take the opportunity to add a `prev_topic` field duplicating `prev_subject` (or maybe better, just switch over to `prev_topic` and then have a bit of code re-add `prev_subject` for clients), so that we're in a position to stop having the database have that legacy field name.
* We'd update the API documentation to document the new `prev_topic` and `new_stream_id` and `topic` fields.

Tagging as a release goal because I think changing this is the simplest path to completing #19919 via #21075, which cannot be done correctly at present without implementing the algorithm we want on the backend, on the frontend.

Server sending mark-unread for already-unread messages

To reproduce:
* Open up the web app in a dev server running https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/21477 .
  * (That provides handy UI for exercising the issue; but the behavior is something the server itself shouldn't allow, and that PR doesn't touch the server, so it's already a bug in main.)
* Watch the events the server emits.
  * One way to do this is in the "Network" tab of Chrome DevTools, while viewing the web app; look at "Preview" for each "events" request.
  * Another is to run a dev build of the mobile app, and use the debug console there.
* Go to some conversation with several messages.
* Mark the first message as unread, with `m` or the three-dots menu.
* Mark that message as unread again.

Expected:
* Each of the `update_message_flags`/`remove`/`read` events should list just the messages for which the `read` flag was removed. As [the API docs](https://zulip.com/api/get-events#update_message_flags-remove) say:
  > `messages`: (integer)[]
  > Array containing the IDs of the messages from which the flag was removed.

Actual:
* Each of those messages lists all of the messages in the conversation, even though most of them are already unread and therefore cannot have the `read` flag removed.
  * (In my experiments, typically one of the messages will be promptly marked as read after marking the whole thread as unread -- either the one at the top where my cursor is, or the next one just after it. That seems like a bug in #21477; certainly the inconsistency where it's sometimes one and sometimes another seems like a bug. Given that web client behavior, that one message has the `read` flag and so that one message is available to participate in a later mark-as-unread event.

    But regardless of the client's behavior, the server is responsible for its event stream: three messages get marked as unread, then just one gets marked as read, then all three get marked again as unread.)

With the current version of https://github.com/zulip/zulip-mobile/pull/4790 -- which I was just about to merge -- this behavior causes the unread counter for the conversation (in the inbox view) to grow larger and larger if you keep doing it, because we accumulate more and more duplicate references to the same message. I might add a workaround in the client before merging that. But we really shouldn't have to work around broken server behavior; it should be fixed in the server.
